utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Moran, I hear your client is not feeling too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been informed by the security personnel for the Tribunal that he was up all night very sick and the Registry has told me he has been examined by a physician this morning. The physician does not want him leaving the detention centre. Apparently he has influenza and is very weak today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Does this actually affect your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem I have is I am unable to waive any of my client's rights without his permission. I have not gotten -- I have not had any communications with him. I cannot in good conscience waive his right to be here without getting his permission to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually I was trying to find out whether you knew anything about it, if you had been in communication with him and to know exactly whether he thinks you can carry on without him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have not been in communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Because it is his right and we acknowledge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I have not -- I was informed of it some time after 9 o'clock this morning by both the Chief of Security and a representative of the Registry. Your Honour, you know exactly what I know. I have not been able to get in touch with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We actually are not too sure about the probable duration of this type of infirmity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am hoping, since I was very close to him yesterday in the conference room, that it is either not very communicable or it is very short. I think Mr. Beresford from the Registry is sitting out in the audience. If I could have maybe a minute to go and confirm with him; he has talked with the physicians. He is also looking quite embarrassed at this point. May I be excused for two or three minutes to talk to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Beresford has just been in contact with the detention centre. The prognosis is that he will not be able to be here today. He will be seen by medical personnel probably this afternoon and we will have a good idea of whether or not he can be here tomorrow some time this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There is nothing we can do with that, him not being able to be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Would the court like me at some point today to go out to the detention centre and get some instructions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think so. That would be a good idea, to know exactly what to do. Actually, in the absence of the trial not going on, I suppose we can do any other business. We have motions which arrived. We might be able to take one or two of them. The one I remember is the motion on the redaction of the statement of the witness. I think we will be able to take that, because all replies have been entered. I think we can hear argument on that. Mr. Ostberg, are you sure you will be able to take that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. McHenry will deal with that. MS.. McHENRY: Your Honour, with respect to the argument on this motion, we would ask that it be held in private session because I believe that talking about the issue and whether or not it should be part of the public record -- I believe the discussion should be private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I raise the question of the schedule for the upcoming days, what is going to happen on Thursday, on Monday next week, etc. We are in a bit of a confusion on the side of the prosecution primarily concerning our witnesses and when we bring them here and when we produce them, which days we can foresee being trial days and which days are not to be trial days. If your Honours have any possibility to enlighten us on that, I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have we not already sent out a notification about the days when we are sitting and when we are not?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: We have not seen any.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think we have received a notification that we are not sitting on Wednesday. I do not know if that is formal. We have not received notification about Wednesday but we have heard that we are not sitting Wednesday. We have received notification about Monday, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Wednesday and Thursday we are sure we are not sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Do we know anything about Thursday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When are the holidays, because there is a request from some counsel for Muslims; they would like to go back and celebrate it. We would like to accommodate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The holidays vary. Somewhere it is 17 and somewhere it is 18. We Muslims cannot agree. MR. KARABDIC (in interpretation): Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think in view of the composition of the accused persons it will not be desirable to argue any motions which in most cases is likely to be affected by their interest and contribution. So for the time being we will have nothing to do. Tomorrow two of my colleagues are joining Judge McDonald in a very interesting argument which they will hear. I think a lot of amicus curiae have been invited, I think about 16 of them are likely to be here -- on the possibility of the Trial Chamber issuing subpoenas against governments and high governmental officials. So tomorrow and Thursday, it is likely those two days these arguments might be on. Earlier we had already indicated that there is likely to be, in the interests of the Muslim counsel and those participating here, the accused persons, a Muslim holiday for Friday and Monday also. We are not taking back that. So we still leave it as it is. We are also praying that during this period no other person catches influenza and that the person already suffering it should recover so that we carry on on Tuesday next week. I think that should be all right for us. That is the programme for the time being. I hope we will find a way of avoiding some of these stoppages, because the earlier we carry on and move efficiently, the better it will be for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Otherwise you will be here until Christmas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So the Trial Chamber will now rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: at 10.00 am) --ooOoo--
